facts.text: The composition was changed from Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 by increasing Fe and Co, decreasing Mn, and reducing P from 20 to 15 at.%.
Arc-solidified material was compared with approximately 20 μm ribbon produced by melt spinning on a copper wheel at 40 m/s.
Arc melting was performed under 99.999% Ar in a water-cooled copper crucible.
DSC heating and cooling measurements were conducted under Ar at 20 K/min.
The compositional modification suppressed primary solid-solution crystallization and high-temperature phosphide formation, shifting solidification toward cooperative eutectic growth.
The slower-cooled ingot developed fine, predominantly rod-like eutectic colonies with Fe–Ni–Mn-rich solid solution regions and P/Cr-rich phosphides.
Rapid melt spinning suppressed elemental segregation and phosphide nucleation sufficiently to retain amorphous order.
Relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the modified alloy showed a simpler and more eutectic-dominated solidification sequence.
XRD showed that the approximately 20 μm melt-spun ribbon was fully amorphous, whereas the slower-cooled ingot was multiphase crystalline.
The amorphous ribbon crystallized in three stages, beginning at 659 K and finishing near 820 K.
The ribbon had a reported crystallization interval ΔTc of approximately 161 K during DSC heating at 20 K/min.
The dominant bulk eutectic exotherm occurred over 1281.9–1256.4 K and released 170.7 J/g.
